# Skyscanner Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/skyscanner-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/skyscanner-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects flight data from Skyscanner, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Skyscanner Flight Prices in Python (2026)](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-skyscanner)
- **Code:** [`skyscanner.py`](skyscanner.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Oneway](results/oneway.json) · [Roundtrip](results/roundtrip.json)

## What it scrapes

- Skyscanner flight search results (one-way and round-trip)
- Carrier, departure/arrival times, duration, stops, price, and provider deal count

## Functions

- `scrape_flights(origin, destination, departure_date, adults=1, cabin_class='economy', return_date=None, market_country='US')` → `FlightSearch`: Scrape Skyscanner one-way or round-trip flight results via XHR interception.

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`FlightResult`**: `origin`, `destination`, `departure_date`, `trip_type`, `market_country`, `currency`, `carrier?`, `operated_by?`, `departure_time?`, `arrival_time?`, `duration?`, `stops?`, `price?`, `provider_deal_count?`, `captured_at`, `return_date`, `return_carrier?`, `return_operated_by?`, `return_departure_time?`, `return_arrival_time?`, `return_duration?`, `return_stops?`
- **`FlightSearch`**: `url`, `origin`, `destination`, `departure_date`, `return_date`, `trip_type`, `market_country`, `flight_count`, `flights`

A field marked `?` can be `null`.

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`skyscanner.py`](skyscanner.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `asp` = `True`: Anti Scraping Protection, the earlier name of the [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker)
- `proxy_pool` = `"public_residential_pool"`: proxy pool (datacenter or residential)
- `render_js` = `True`: render the page in a real browser
- `rendering_wait` = `5000`: wait after the page rendered, in milliseconds
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/skyscanner-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_scrape_flights_oneway`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
